clue.text: A bird, one that's fluttering and jaunty

indicators.note: something fluttering flaps about and is unsettled, so these letters are shaken into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cheerful bird flaps about, looking jaunty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' rearranges the letters of A BIRD ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone stylish, carefree and confident in manner.

clue.text: Her underwear — a species of bloomers

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman, a lady's
a slip is a woman's undergarment
a, as in 'so much a head', means per

explanation.surface: A woman's underwear is described as a kind of bloomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like knickers to match the underwear, but here it means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a kind of orchid, and a flower is something that blooms.

clue.text: Understood 'mischief-maker's staying within the law

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little sprite; the 's is no letter
licit means lawful, permitted

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is said, by unspoken agreement, to be keeping on the right side of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied but not stated is tacitly grasped, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Sixth sense initially of use to champion

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is often called the sixth sense

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gift for intuition is said to help a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champion' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb: to support a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to take it up and support it, a synonym.

clue.text: Is stunning woman over there OK?

parts.note: KO is a knockout, stunning someone; KO's reads as 'KO is'
her points to a woman, someone over there

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a gorgeous woman across the room is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunning' looks like praise for the woman, but it is a knockout punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Kosher is informal for genuine or acceptable, an idiom matching 'all right'.

clue.text: Cargo-boat with accommodation for child

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used for carrying goods in the Baltic
a baby carriage that a child rides in

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the Baltic lighter and the pushchair for a baby.

clue.text: Show how to repeat changes

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the words before it are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone explains how to perform a repeat, with alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges TO REPEAT; 'how' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera is a kind of stage show, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Avalanche perhaps, covering borders in spring

definitions.text: Avalanche perhaps, covering borders in spring

parts.words: Avalanche perhaps, covering borders in spring
parts.note: an avalanche is literally a fall of snow, and this small white flower carpets garden beds early in the year

explanation.surface: A snow slide blankets the edges of something in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' are flower beds, not frontiers, and 'spring' is the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower name splits into a fall of snow, and the plant blooms in garden beds early in the year.

clue.text: Jack and Edward are retired

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is another
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Two men, Jack and Edward, have stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like stopped working; here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire can mean to go to bed for the night, so someone in bed has retired.

clue.text: Bunting adding colour to sledge

parts.note: yellow is a colour
a sledge is a sledgehammer

explanation.surface: Someone paints a sledge to brighten it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' looks like flags; it is a family of small songbirds. 'sledge' looks like a toboggan.
explanation.definitionFit: This songbird belongs to the bunting family, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Banter from mouse, rather cute

parts.note: Mickey is the famous cartoon mouse
taking means attractive, charming

explanation.surface: Teasing remarks come from a sweet little mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the mickey is British slang for making fun of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing someone in fun is the idiom's meaning, so it matches playful banter.

clue.text: Capers about far in the distance

indicators.note: about signals that the word before it is turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Antics take place a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CAPERS. 'far in the' is read here as a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical unit of length, about 3.26 light years, so it is a measure of distance.

clue.text: It helps to drive army unit back north, out of the county

indicators.note: back says the army word is written in reverse

parts.note: a corps is a unit of an army

indicators.note: out of says one letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: Kent, the Garden of England, is a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: An army unit retreats northwards, leaving the county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CORPS into SPROC; 'out of' takes N from KENT, leaving KET.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel engages a chain to turn a bicycle or film reel, so it helps drive machinery.

clue.text: Try and fail, unfortunately revealing weakness

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Attempting something and failing exposes a weak spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges TRY and FAIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailty is lack of strength, physical or moral, a synonym.

clue.text: Looking for iron found in US state? On 'the contrary, given up

indicators.note: found in would put the metal inside the state
on the contrary reverses that, so the state goes inside the metal

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Oregon is a state in the north-west USA

explanation.surface: Someone prospecting for iron in an American state abandons the search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking for' is read here as a link phrase; the surface prospector is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Foregone, or forgone, means gone without, renounced, a synonym of relinquished.

clue.text: Lamb chasing ball hit up into plant

indicators.note: chasing means the writer's name comes after the stroke

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high in the air
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A lamb runs after a ball lofted into a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' looks like a young sheep; it is the writer Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Total inaccurate? Accurate

parts.note: a guess that is out is wrong
right means correct

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a total is wrong and is told it is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means complete, absolute, as in an outright win, a synonym.

clue.text: Visionary thought brought to heel

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship heels or lists when it leans over

explanation.surface: A notion is brought to heel like a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like the foot or a dog command; it is a ship leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer with lofty, often unrealistic aims is a visionary, a synonym.

clue.text: Young Sherlock Holmes, say, almost finishing homework, sounded calm

indicators.note: finishing places the next piece at the end
almost means the last letter of the school word is dropped

parts.note: prep is school homework

indicators.note: sounded means the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to quell is to calm or subdue

explanation.surface: A youthful detective almost finishes his homework and keeps calm.
explanation.walkthrough: PREP is British school slang for homework; 'almost' cuts it to PRE. QUEL sounds like QUELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A story about the detective's youth is set before the original tales, an example of a prequel.

clue.text: Cut down tree to show how it may spring up again?

parts.note: to reap is to cut down a crop
a pear is a fruit tree

explanation.surface: A tree is felled to show how it might grow back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to show how it may' is read here as a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to come back into view, which is what springing up again means.

clue.text: Rod raised hat he was a mathematician

indicators.note: raised in a down clue says the rod word is written upward, in reverse

parts.note: a cue is a billiard player's rod
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A man with a rod lifts his hat; he was a mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns CUE into EUC; 'he was a' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of the Elements, the classic geometry text, was a mathematician.

clue.text: Headgear fitter for recycling

indicators.note: something sent for recycling is broken down and remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor's hat is sent off to be recycled.
explanation.walkthrough: TITFER is rhyming slang (tit for tat = hat).
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang for a hat, so it is an item of headgear.

clue.text: Examination of river

definitions.meaning: the river in Hampshire that flows past Romsey into Southampton Water

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a trial and the name of an English river.

clue.text: Wading bird is found round the outskirts of Bali

indicators.note: found round says the short word wraps around the letters that follow
the outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A wading bird turns up at the edge of Bali.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found round' looks like discovery nearby, but it signals one piece wrapping another.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged bird with a curved bill that wades in marshes.

clue.text: I have investigated first sudden drop

indicators.note: first means the snooping word comes before the other piece

parts.note: nosed around means investigated
I've is short for I have

explanation.surface: Someone admits they looked into a sudden fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunge, of an aircraft or of prices, is a steep sudden fall, a synonym.

clue.text: Sue brightened up one entrance

parts.note: lit up means brightened
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Sue's face lit up when someone came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name; it is the legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to take someone to court, which is to go to law.
